title: Medically Tailored Meal Trial for MASH Patients
official: Medically Tailored Meal Trial for MASH Patients
summary: Fatty liver disease is a major problem in the United States. Over 30% of all people and over 40% of Hispanics have fatty liver, and this number is continuing to rise due to the obesity epidemic. Fatty liver can be benign or aggressive. When it becomes aggressive by causing inflammation in the liver, it is called metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, or MASH, and can lead to liver cirrhosis and liver cancer. Therefore, it is very important to find solutions to prevent MASH from becoming worse. While a healthy diet and weight loss are the best ways to prevent and even improve MASH, maintaining a healthy diet can be difficult for people who are experiencing food insecurity or who have limited access to nutritious foods due to lack of financial resources. Healthy food delivery programs have been shown to improve diet-sensitive diseases, including diabetes and heart failure, in people who are food insecure. They similarly have the potential to benefit people with MASH but have never been studied in this population. This study proposes a 12-week culturally tailored medically meal program for food-insecure participants who live in Los Angeles County and are seen at the Keck Liver Clinic. The goals of this study are to assess acceptability of the program, as well as improvements in food insecurity, diet quality, liver inflammation, and diabetes risk. Secondary goals are to study whether changes in diet quality can be sustained for several months after completing the meal delivery program. The overall aim of this study is to develop new programs that provide healthy foods and dietary education to people who cannot afford them with the goal of improving fatty liver and other diet-sensitive related conditions for people in Los Angeles.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults ≥18 years with MASH who screen positive for food insecurity using the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Household Food Security Survey (HFSS)
* MASH is defined as hepatic steatosis (CAP≥263 dB/M) with ≥F1 fibrosis (liver stiffness measurement of ≥6 kilopascals), elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT; \>20 for women or \>35 for men), and ≥1 of 5 cardiometabolic criteria: (1) BMI ≥25 kg/m2 (or ≥23 kg/m2 if Asian) OR waist circumference \>94 cm for males and \>80 cm for females, (2) fasting serum glucose ≥100 mg/dL OR 2-hour post-load glucose levels ≥140 mg/dL OR HbA1c ≥5.7% OR type 2 diabetes diagnosis OR treatment, (3) blood pressure ≥130/85 mmHg OR specific antihypertensive drug treatment, (4) plasma triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL or on lipid lowering treatment, or (5) plasma HDL ≤40 mg/dL for men or ≤50 mg/dL for women OR on lipid lowering treatment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Heavy alcohol use (average daily alcohol intake \>20-50 g in women, \>30-60 g in men in the past 12 months); and
* Participants living outside of Los Angeles County (i.e. \>25-mile radius outside of the Project Angel Food Hub)
